unavailable_fields.nvlink_bytes: NVML nvmlDeviceGetNvLinkState returned status 3 on both GPUs (capability probes); per-link counters unsupported, and NCCL channels are observed as SHM/direct/direct, so no NVLink traffic dimension exists to collect.
unavailable_fields.per_collective_pcie_bytes: device_telemetry NVML pcie.tx/rx are device-wide rates in native ~20ms driver sampling windows not aligned to collective ranges; probe rates are not workload traffic, and logical payload sizes must not be converted into traffic.
unavailable_fields.nccl_wire_time_ms: No collector separates in-kernel NCCL waiting from wire transfer; device kernel durations and nsys timelines both include waiting, so wire time stays unknown.
unavailable_fields.hardware_utilization: Hardware counters require a successful collector-specific probe; topology and logical payload do not measure traffic (status unknown in capability probes).

plan.rationale: The torch collector already ran and fixed the objective evidence: communication_kernel_sum_ms is 325.667 ms on rank 0 vs 63.633 ms on rank 1 (max-rank aggregation picks rank 0), from 13 fully matched fp32 allreduces (12 buckets of 28,351,488 bytes plus the 157,541,376-byte last bucket), all ncclDevKernel_AllReduce_Sum_f32_RING_LL on stream 17 over SHM/direct/direct with peer access disabled and every bucket attributed via observed gradient-storage membership. Identical 27 MiB buckets cost ~13.4-13.7 ms on rank 0 but only ~3.56-3.63 ms on rank 1, the first rank-0 kernel lasts 156.3 ms, and compute overlap is only ~6.7 of 325.7 ms, so the max-rank metric is dominated by in-kernel waiting for the slower rank, not by transfer. The plan therefore targets rank-skew attribution and NCCL algorithm/protocol decisions: execution_timeline for CPU-submit-to-CUDA associations, synchronization and per-device intervals plus passive post-accumulate callbacks to locate when buckets become ready on each rank (its CPU-submission clock-alignment bounds leave GPU readiness unknown); nsys (available on both ranks) for a unified single-host cross-rank timeline to attribute rank-0 kernel waits to peer arrival versus execution, which the per-rank torch traces cannot support because their clock policy forbids cross-rank timestamp subtraction; nccl_tuning because kernel entry names alone do not identify the protocol and it captures the actual warmed-worker NCCL algorithm/protocol/channel decisions at the observed 28,351,488- and 157,541,376-byte fp32 sizes, the direct lever on kernel duration; collective_calibration as a warmed full-world SUM allreduce reference at exactly the observed sizes/dtypes to separate intrinsic collective cost from wait-inclusive durations (reference only, not a lower bound or critical-path estimate). Excluded: device_telemetry (device-wide NVML rates in native windows, NVLink counters unsupported status 3, cannot attribute per-collective traffic and would not inform kernel-duration reduction); python_runtime (perturbs execution and yields host cProfile times, not GPU durations; host dispatch is not implicated by the trace evidence); binding_cost and candidate_diagnostics (no candidate exists yet at planning stage, and bundle-replacing candidates would make binding_cost inapplicable); torch (already ran and produced the objective field communication_kernel_sum_ms).

usage.scope: Observed assistant message snapshots; provider estimates, not invoice
